idiom_name: container method taking a std::function/lambda + std::copy_if into a new container
implementation_notes: C++11 supplies the criterion as a value - lambda, function object or std::function - and std::copy_if applies it, so the pattern is realised as a container method that accepts (or stores) the predicate and returns a new container of the same type: System filtered(const std::function<bool(const Threat&)>& keep) const, building the result with std::copy_if. The std::function wrapper is what makes the criterion a stored first-class object behind one signature and lets heterogeneous criteria live in one place, at the price of a type-erased call; a template parameter or plain lambda avoids that indirection when the criterion is used once. Choose this form for C++11/14/17 toolchains and when the API must return a real container rather than a view.
pitfalls: std::function type-erases the criterion and adds an indirect call (plus a possible allocation) per invocation; pass a template parameter or a non-owning function reference when the predicate is hot or used once.
std::copy_if copies the elements, so the filtered container owns copies (or smart pointers); for heavy elements prefer indices, spans or a view instead of duplicating the payload.

A predicate captured by reference ([&]) dangles as soon as it escapes the scope that owns the captured state - storing it in a std::function member and returning the container is the classic version of this bug.

variants.name: Lazy composable filter with std::views::filter (C++20)
variants.implementation_notes: C++20 ranges make the filter object part of the library: threats | std::views::filter(pred) builds a filter_view that stores the predicate (exposed through pred()) and yields matching elements on demand, so several filters compose without intermediate containers; materialise with a range constructor or with C++23 std::ranges::to<std::vector>() when a container-typed copy is required. Prefer this for pipelines and large inputs; the predicate is re-invoked on every traversal, and mutating an element of a forward-range filter_view so that it no longer satisfies the predicate is undefined behaviour.
pitfalls: The predicate is re-run on every traversal (only the begin iterator of a forward range is cached), so a stateful or expensive criterion must be hoisted out of the view or the view materialised once.
Treat a filter_view as read-only: modifying an element of a forward-range view so that it stops satisfying the predicate is undefined behaviour.
Views do not own their data: a filter_view that outlives the range or the predicate it was built from dangles, which makes returning views from functions a lifetime hazard.
